disclaimer: Prototype IPM guidance. Not a pesticide prescription. Follow locally approved recommendations and product labels.

fallback.immediate_action: Inspect several plants in different parts of the field and note how fast symptoms are spreading.
fallback.cultural_control: Improve field sanitation, manage crop residue, and avoid practices that keep foliage wet for long periods.
fallback.mechanical_control: Remove heavily affected plant parts where practical and dispose of them away from the crop.
fallback.biological_control: Ask the local extension officer about locally recommended biological options.
fallback.monitoring: Re-check the field every 2–3 days and keep a simple record of new spots or pests.
fallback.chemical_control_category: Use chemical products only if locally registered for this crop/problem and only when intervention is justified. Do not invent a dose or brand.
fallback.safety_notes: Use PPE, follow the product label, and observe pre-harvest intervals. Keep children and livestock away during application.
fallback.when_to_contact_officer: Contact the agriculture extension officer if the problem is spreading rapidly or the diagnosis is uncertain.

tomato_early_blight.immediate_action: Inspect nearby plants for brown concentric leaf spots. Remove severely affected lower leaves if recommended locally.
tomato_early_blight.cultural_control: Avoid overhead watering late in the day. Improve air flow. Rotate away from tomato/potato where possible.
tomato_early_blight.mechanical_control: Remove and destroy heavily diseased foliage; do not compost if local guidance advises against it.
tomato_early_blight.biological_control: Ask about locally approved bio-fungicide options; do not substitute unverified products.
tomato_early_blight.monitoring: Check lower leaves twice a week during humid weather.
tomato_early_blight.chemical_control_category: If pressure is high, use only locally registered protectant/systemic products for early blight as per label.
tomato_early_blight.safety_notes: Never mix products without label support. Observe PHI. This app does not recommend a brand or dose.
tomato_early_blight.when_to_contact_officer: Contact extension if fruit lesions appear or several rows are affected.

tomato_late_blight.immediate_action: Treat as high priority in cool, wet weather. Inspect the whole block the same day.
tomato_late_blight.cultural_control: Reduce leaf wetness. Avoid working in wet fields. Destroy volunteer potato/tomato plants.
tomato_late_blight.mechanical_control: Remove badly infected plants to slow spread if practical.
tomato_late_blight.biological_control: Biological options are limited; seek local specialist advice.
tomato_late_blight.monitoring: Walk the field after rain. Look for water-soaked lesions and white growth on leaf undersides.
tomato_late_blight.chemical_control_category: Late blight may justify timely use of locally registered products. Follow label only.
tomato_late_blight.safety_notes: PPE and label restrictions are mandatory. Do not use leftover unlabelled chemicals.
tomato_late_blight.when_to_contact_officer: Notify the officer immediately if multiple farms in the village show similar symptoms.

tomato_healthy.immediate_action: No disease action required from this image. Continue routine scouting.
tomato_healthy.cultural_control: Maintain balanced nutrition and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
tomato_healthy.monitoring: Scout weekly; increase frequency in humid weather.
tomato_healthy.chemical_control_category: Do not spray preventively without a local recommendation.
tomato_healthy.when_to_contact_officer: Contact extension if new spots appear suddenly after storms.

potato_early_blight.immediate_action: Inspect older leaves for target-like spots. Note irrigation timing.
potato_early_blight.cultural_control: Avoid water stress. Hill soil to protect tubers. Rotate crops.
potato_early_blight.mechanical_control: Remove severely blighted haulm if locally advised.
potato_early_blight.biological_control: Discuss bio-fungicide options with the KVK/extension office.
potato_early_blight.monitoring: Check weekly from vegetative stage onward.
potato_early_blight.chemical_control_category: Use only registered early-blight products if thresholds and weather justify it.
potato_early_blight.safety_notes: Follow label PPE and harvest waiting periods.
potato_early_blight.when_to_contact_officer: Call if lesions move onto stems or many plants yellow quickly.

potato_late_blight.immediate_action: This is a fast-spreading disease in wet weather. Scout the entire field today.
potato_late_blight.cultural_control: Destroy cull piles and volunteers. Avoid irrigation that keeps leaves wet overnight.
potato_late_blight.mechanical_control: Roguing of badly infected plants may slow local spread.
potato_late_blight.monitoring: Daily checks during cool rainy spells.
potato_late_blight.chemical_control_category: May require locally registered late-blight products used strictly as labelled.
potato_late_blight.safety_notes: Do not share unverified spray schedules. No dose is provided here.
potato_late_blight.when_to_contact_officer: Report village-level outbreaks so neighbours can scout too.

potato_healthy.immediate_action: Continue good crop care. No treatment indicated from this image.
potato_healthy.cultural_control: Keep drainage good and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

cotton_pink_bollworm.immediate_action: Inspect squares and bolls. Look for exit holes and stained lint.
cotton_pink_bollworm.cultural_control: Timely sowing, clean-up of leftover bolls, and destruction of crop residue after harvest.
cotton_pink_bollworm.mechanical_control: Collect and destroy infested bolls where practical. Use pheromone monitoring if available locally.
cotton_pink_bollworm.biological_control: Ask about locally recommended biocontrol / ETL-based IPM packages.
cotton_pink_bollworm.monitoring: Check 20 plants in a zigzag walk. Record damaged fruiting bodies.
cotton_pink_bollworm.chemical_control_category: Apply insecticides only if local ETL is crossed and only with registered products for this pest.
cotton_pink_bollworm.safety_notes: Protect pollinators. Do not spray during peak bee activity. No brand or dose is given here.
cotton_pink_bollworm.when_to_contact_officer: Contact extension if damage is rising across several fields.

cotton_aphids.immediate_action: Check undersides of young leaves for colonies and sticky honeydew.
cotton_aphids.cultural_control: Avoid excessive nitrogen. Conserve natural enemies by not spraying unnecessarily.
cotton_aphids.mechanical_control: A strong water jet can dislodge small colonies on young plants if water is available.
cotton_aphids.biological_control: Ladybird beetles and other predators often suppress aphids. Ask about local biocontrol options.
cotton_aphids.monitoring: Inspect tender shoots twice a week.
cotton_aphids.chemical_control_category: Treat only if populations exceed local ETL. Prefer selective options recommended locally.
cotton_aphids.safety_notes: Broad-spectrum sprays can worsen outbreaks by killing predators.
cotton_aphids.when_to_contact_officer: Call if sooty mould is covering large canopy areas.

cotton_whitefly.immediate_action: Inspect lower leaf surfaces. Note yellowing and sticky residue.
cotton_whitefly.cultural_control: Avoid continuous cotton–cotton cropping. Manage weeds that host whitefly.
cotton_whitefly.mechanical_control: Yellow sticky traps can help monitoring, not full control.
cotton_whitefly.biological_control: Protect parasitoids. Ask KVK for locally recommended biological tools.
cotton_whitefly.monitoring: Count adults on lower leaves in the morning.
cotton_whitefly.chemical_control_category: If ETL is crossed, use only registered products and rotate modes of action as locally advised.
cotton_whitefly.safety_notes: Whitefly resistance is common; do not repeat the same product blindly. No dose listed here.
cotton_whitefly.when_to_contact_officer: Report if neighbouring fields also show sudden increase.

cotton_healthy.immediate_action: No pest action indicated. Continue routine scouting.
cotton_healthy.cultural_control: Keep field borders clean and avoid unnecessary sprays.
cotton_healthy.when_to_contact_officer: Contact if sticky leaves or square shedding increases.

maize_fall_armyworm.immediate_action: Inspect 10–20 plants in representative areas, especially the whorl.
maize_fall_armyworm.cultural_control: Timely sowing in windows recommended locally. Destroy crop residues after harvest.
maize_fall_armyworm.mechanical_control: Hand-crush egg masses and young larvae where labour allows. Remove heavily infested plants if practical.
maize_fall_armyworm.biological_control: Consider locally recommended biological control options (e.g. approved biopesticides) — ask the extension officer.
maize_fall_armyworm.monitoring: Look for egg masses, window-pane feeding, and frass in the whorl twice a week.
maize_fall_armyworm.chemical_control_category: Use only locally registered products and label-approved directions when intervention thresholds justify it.
maize_fall_armyworm.safety_notes: Use appropriate PPE. Observe label restrictions and pre-harvest intervals. No brand or dose is provided.
maize_fall_armyworm.when_to_contact_officer: Contact the agriculture extension officer if infestation is spreading rapidly.

maize_leaf_blight.immediate_action: Note how far lesions have moved up the plant. Check hybrids in adjacent plots.
maize_leaf_blight.cultural_control: Crop rotation and residue management. Avoid dense planting that keeps leaves wet.
maize_leaf_blight.mechanical_control: Not usually practical at field scale; focus on sanitation at small-plot level.
maize_leaf_blight.monitoring: Scout weekly from vegetative stage, especially after rain.
maize_leaf_blight.chemical_control_category: Fungicide use only if locally recommended for this disease and crop stage.
maize_leaf_blight.safety_notes: Follow label. No concentration or mixing instructions are given here.
maize_leaf_blight.when_to_contact_officer: Call if lesions reach the ear leaf before grain fill.

maize_healthy.immediate_action: Continue standard scouting. No treatment indicated.
maize_healthy.cultural_control: Maintain balanced fertility and good drainage.
maize_healthy.monitoring: Check whorls for armyworm after storms.
maize_healthy.when_to_contact_officer: Contact if ragged whorl damage appears.

rice_blast.immediate_action: Inspect leaves and necks. Note water management and nitrogen use.
rice_blast.cultural_control: Avoid excess nitrogen. Maintain recommended water levels. Use resistant varieties if available locally.
rice_blast.mechanical_control: Not usually practical; remove severely infected nursery seedlings if spotted early.
rice_blast.biological_control: Discuss locally recommended biocontrol / bio-fungicide options with extension staff.
rice_blast.monitoring: Watch for diamond-shaped leaf spots after cloudy, humid weather.
rice_blast.chemical_control_category: If blast is increasing, use only registered rice products as per label and local advisory.
rice_blast.safety_notes: Protect water bodies. Do not apply unlabelled chemicals to paddy water.
rice_blast.when_to_contact_officer: Report neck blast risk at heading immediately.

rice_brown_spot.immediate_action: Check whether plants are nutrient-stressed, especially potassium and other locally deficient nutrients.
rice_brown_spot.cultural_control: Balanced fertilization and good drainage. Use healthy seed.
rice_brown_spot.biological_control: Ask about seed treatment options recommended locally.
rice_brown_spot.monitoring: Compare low-lying vs well-drained parts of the field.
rice_brown_spot.chemical_control_category: Chemical use only if local guidance supports it after correcting nutrition/water issues.
rice_brown_spot.safety_notes: Brown spot is often linked to crop stress — do not jump to pesticides first.
rice_brown_spot.when_to_contact_officer: Contact if many grains are discoloured.

rice_healthy.immediate_action: No disease action indicated. Keep routine nursery/field checks.
rice_healthy.cultural_control: Balanced nutrients and recommended water management.
rice_healthy.when_to_contact_officer: Call if sudden leaf spots appear at tillering or heading.

wheat_rust.immediate_action: Inspect leaves for rust pustules. Note wind direction from neighbouring fields.
wheat_rust.cultural_control: Prefer locally recommended varieties. Avoid late sowing if that is a local risk factor.
wheat_rust.biological_control: Limited; rely on variety and timely local advisories.
wheat_rust.monitoring: Scout weekly from stem elongation. Rust can increase quickly.
wheat_rust.chemical_control_category: If locally recommended at this growth stage, use only registered products as labelled.
wheat_rust.safety_notes: No dose or brand is provided. Observe harvest intervals.
wheat_rust.when_to_contact_officer: Report if pustules are widespread so the district can be alerted.

wheat_powdery_mildew.immediate_action: Check dense canopies and shaded parts of the field.
wheat_powdery_mildew.cultural_control: Avoid excess nitrogen. Improve airflow with recommended spacing.
wheat_powdery_mildew.biological_control: Ask extension about locally approved options.
wheat_powdery_mildew.monitoring: Look for white powdery growth on lower leaves.
wheat_powdery_mildew.chemical_control_category: Treat only if local thresholds and crop stage justify a registered product.
wheat_powdery_mildew.safety_notes: Follow label PPE. No mixing instructions here.
wheat_powdery_mildew.when_to_contact_officer: Contact if mildew reaches the flag leaf.

wheat_healthy.immediate_action: Continue routine scouting. No treatment indicated.
wheat_healthy.cultural_control: Balanced fertility and recommended sowing time.
wheat_healthy.monitoring: Weekly rust watch during cool humid periods.

soybean_mosaic_virus.immediate_action: Look for mosaic patterns and check for aphids that can spread viruses.
soybean_mosaic_virus.cultural_control: Use healthy seed. Manage weeds. Avoid working from infected to healthy plots.
soybean_mosaic_virus.mechanical_control: Rogue severely affected plants in small plots if practical.
soybean_mosaic_virus.biological_control: Conserve aphid predators. Virus itself is not treated with insecticide as a cure.
soybean_mosaic_virus.monitoring: Walk rows weekly. Note patchy yellow mosaic.
soybean_mosaic_virus.chemical_control_category: Insecticides do not cure virus. Aphid management only if locally advised for vector control.
soybean_mosaic_virus.safety_notes: Do not spray hoping to 'kill the virus'. Seek expert confirmation.
soybean_mosaic_virus.when_to_contact_officer: Request expert/lab confirmation — virus symptoms can resemble nutrient issues.

soybean_rust.immediate_action: Inspect lower leaves for small pustules. Note recent humidity and rain.
soybean_rust.cultural_control: Avoid dense canopies if possible. Follow local sowing guidance.
soybean_rust.monitoring: Scout lower canopy after humid nights.
soybean_rust.chemical_control_category: If rust is confirmed and local advisory supports it, use registered products as labelled.
soybean_rust.safety_notes: No brand, dose, or tank-mix is provided.
soybean_rust.when_to_contact_officer: Contact if pustules are increasing quickly during flowering/pod fill.

soybean_healthy.immediate_action: No disease action indicated. Continue scouting.
soybean_healthy.when_to_contact_officer: Call if mosaic or rust-like pustules appear.
